question_text: Forests precede civilizations and deserts follow them.
customKeyPointers: A civilisation starts by using a living landscape
It ends when it has used that landscape up
The desert in the line is often a consequence, not a climate

points.text: The sentence puts a forest before a civilisation and a desert after it, as if the middle term were the thing that used the first up.
Settled life begins where there is wood, soil and water. The city is built out of that stock.

When the cutting, the grazing and the salt of a bad irrigation go on longer than the land can recover, the same place becomes barren. Several old centres are now dust beside the record of their glory.
Not every desert was made by a city. The line is still a true warning about the ones that were.
A modern economy that treats a forest as only a store of timber is repeating the sequence with better tools.
Civilisations last when they leave the forest standing. The desert is what follows the refusal.

question_text: The empires of the future will be the empires of the mind.
customKeyPointers: The next dominance is of knowledge, not of territory
Such an empire can be freer, and it can also be more intrusive
A people that does not cultivate its minds will live inside someone else's

points.text: The line says that the power which will matter next is the power to know, to invent and to shape what others think.
Land can be taken and lost. A scientific capacity, a language and a platform that everyone else must use are harder to seize and easier to keep.
The empires already forming are of the chip, the model and the story. They do not need to plant a flag.
An empire of the mind can educate, and it can also capture attention so completely that the subject does not notice the rule.
For a country the implication is blunt: schools, research and a free argument are now instruments of power.
The future empire is whoever owns the minds that others have to rent.

question_text: There is no path to happiness; happiness is the path.
customKeyPointers: The usual error is to postpone happiness until a result arrives
The manner of walking is the thing itself
A cruel means cannot be a path to a happy end

points.text: The sentence refuses the idea that happiness is a prize waiting at the end of a grim road.
If the path is anxiety, comparison and a postponed life, the arrival, when it comes, is only the next postponement.
Happiness as the path means attention, a proportion and a way of treating people that is already the condition one was seeking.
A state that promises welfare by a present cruelty makes the same mistake. The method is the outcome, arriving early.
The line is not an excuse for having no aim. It is a warning that the aim will resemble the way it was pursued.
There is no path to happiness that is not itself a way of being happy.

question_text: The doubter is a true man of science.
customKeyPointers: Science begins by not being sure
The doubter asks what would prove the claim wrong
Doubt is a method, not a pose of disbelief
A science without doubters becomes a dogma with instruments

points.text: The true person of science is not the one who knows. It is the one who knows how the claim could fail.
A result that cannot be doubted cannot be tested. Doubt is the condition of an experiment.
The doubter is loyal to the evidence, including the evidence that embarrasses his own school.
This is different from a refusal to believe anything. That is only a slower dogma.
Public life needs the same habit: a policy that cannot say what would show it to be wrong is not a scientific policy.
The doubter is the true man of science because he keeps the claim answerable.

question_text: Social media is triggering a 'fear of missing out' amongst the youth, precipitating depression and loneliness.
customKeyPointers: The feed shows other people's edited lives, continuously
Fear of missing out is the feeling that one's own hour is lesser
The harm is the comparison, not the existence of a screen

points.text: Social media puts a young person in a crowd that never ends and never tells the truth about itself.
Every highlight of someone else arrives as evidence that one is elsewhere, late, or less. That is the fear of missing out.
The fear does not send the person toward friends. It sends him back to the feed, which is why the loneliness grows beside the connection.
Depression follows when the comparison becomes the measure of a day, and the day keeps failing it.
The medium is not fate. A use with a limit and a real room of people is a different thing from a life conducted as an audience.
The trigger is real. What it precipitates is a loneliness that looks, from the outside, like company.

question_text: Nearly all men can stand adversity, but to test the character, give him power.
subTopics: Power as the test of character
customKeyPointers: Adversity shows endurance. Power shows what a person does when he need not endure
Character is what remains when punishment is unlikely
Public life is full of people who passed the first test and failed the second

points.text: Lincoln's line says that suffering is a lesser test than the freedom to hurt, to take, or to be unfair without a cost.
Almost anyone can be dignified in a difficulty, because the difficulty itself supplies the discipline.
Power removes it. The character is then whatever the person does with a file, a budget or a silence that nobody can challenge.
This is why a good private man can be a bad holder of office, and why the office is the fairer examination.
Institutions exist to make the test less absolute: a power that is watched reveals less of the worst, and also less of the best.
To know a character, do not only watch it suffer. Watch it when it can refuse to.

question_text: All ideas having large consequences are always simple.
customKeyPointers: A large consequence needs an idea that many people can carry
Simplicity is what lets it travel
The carrying out is rarely as simple as the sentence
A simple idea can also be a simple cruelty

points.text: Ideas that move a great many lives tend to be sayable in a line. That is the truth in the sentence.
Equality, a right, a market, a nation: each is simple enough to be repeated, and each has rearranged the world.
The consequence is large because the idea can be held by people who will never read the argument behind it.
Always is too strong. Some large results come from a technical idea almost nobody can state, and some simple ideas produce only a slogan.
Simplicity is also how a dangerous idea spreads. A large consequence is not a certificate of truth.
The ideas with large consequences are usually simple. They are not, for that reason, always right.

question_text: The cost of being wrong is less than the cost of doing nothing.
customKeyPointers: Inaction feels free because its cost is delayed and unnamed
A wrong act can be seen and corrected
Doing nothing is itself a decision, usually in favour of the present harm
The line is not a licence for a reckless act

points.text: The sentence compares two prices and finds the visible mistake cheaper than the invisible refusal to move.
A wrong policy can be reversed once its result is seen. A decision not to decide lets the harm continue and calls the continuation caution.
In a famine, a pandemic or a failing institution, the cost of waiting is paid by people who were not in the meeting.
The comparison fails when the wrong act is irreversible: a war, a destroyed forest, a liberty taken and not returned.
The useful reading is to act where the error can be corrected, and to refuse the comfort of doing nothing where the cost is already running.
Being wrong is often cheaper than doing nothing. It is not cheaper than thinking first.
